name: Spine Road Apartments
headline: Spine Road Apartments is a 65-home affordable rental community for households at 30% to 70% AMI at 4775 Spine Road in Boulder's Gunbarrel area, developed by Koelbel and Company with the Boulder County Housing Authority as part of a larger mixed-income site; it won $973,572 a year in 2022 federal 4% credit with $13.35M of CHFA bonds, but financing only closed in June 2026.
why_it_matters: Nearly four years passed between the 2022 credit cycle and closing, with the unit count growing from 59 to 65 and a $3.25M state cash flow loan added in 2024, so it is a live example of how long small 4% deals in high-cost markets can take to assemble.

status.label: Financing closed June 2026; construction expected to start June 2026; completion targeted Q4 2027
status.detail: Koelbel announced on 2026-06-16 that financing had closed and that construction was expected to begin that month, with completion in Q4 2027. No dated building permit or groundbreaking record was found to confirm work is under way.

next_step: Look for a City of Boulder building permit or groundbreaking announcement for 4775 Spine Road.

background.text: The affordable rentals are one piece of a larger 9.87-acre Koelbel site at 4775, 4725 and 4649 Spine Road approved by the City of Boulder for 230 attached homes plus community uses; in November 2023 the Planning Board considered extending that approval.
Koelbel describes it as the first dedicated affordable rental community in Gunbarrel and its 12th affordable project since 2011.
The project grew from 59 units in the 2022 bond letter of intent to 65 units at award and closing.
RTD's Route J is expected to return to the area when the project is complete, per the developer.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2022 Round One or Round Two competitive application narratives; it was a rolling 4% bond deal only.

CHFA's 4% award report says it leaves out developments whose IRS Form 8609s have been issued; this deal is still listed on the 2026-09-21 report, so 8609s had not been issued by then (inferred from the report's note).

timeline.event: Letter of intent to CHFA's 2022 4% bond pool: 59 units, $11M requested
City of Boulder Planning Board hearing on extending Site and Use Review LUR2020-00063
State Housing Board awards a $3.25M cash flow loan
Financing closes; construction expected to start (announced 2026-06-16)
Still listed on CHFA's Federal 4% award report

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the federal 4% credit under cycle year 2022, while the Division of Housing release says the project was awarded 4% federal tax credits in 2023.
The Division of Housing release describes eight three-story buildings, while Koelbel's closing release describes eight two-story buildings.

The Division of Housing release calls Gunbarrel an unincorporated community governed by Boulder County, while the site's land use review was heard by the City of Boulder Planning Board and the City of Boulder is a funding partner.
CHFA's award report lists only 30% and 60% AMI units, while the developer describes the homes as serving households between 30% and 70% AMI.
